title: Teller and Sakharov meet; Sakharov says Teller was right
summary: John Brandenburg tells of Teller and Sakharov meet; Sakharov says Teller was right, about 1950s; later meeting at United States (no place named), and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: And later Teller and Sakharov actually got to meet. And Sakharov, the father of the Russian hydrogen bomb, looked at all of Teller's communications back and forth and said, "Oh, Teller was right.

plain: Physicist John Brandenburg tells Jesse Michels that Edward Teller, a scientist linked to the American hydrogen bomb, later met Andrei Sakharov, whom he calls the father of the Russian hydrogen bomb. According to Brandenburg, Sakharov looked over Teller's back and forth communications and said, "Oh, Teller was right." Brandenburg tells it in support of his larger argument about nuclear science and its hidden history.
